html:
French Algeria was the coast and hinterland of Algeria under French rule. On the 1880 map it covers the settled north, fifty years after the conquest began.

France attacked Algiers in 1830, ending the old Ottoman regency. Inland, Emir Abdelkader led a long resistance until he surrendered in 1847. The war was brutal, with burned villages and famine. In 1848 the north was made into departments of France itself.

By 1880 European settlers, later called pieds-noirs, held much of the best farmland, taken after revolts such as the great Kabyle rising of 1871. A decree in 1870 made Algeria's Jews French citizens. Most Muslims stayed subjects without a vote, under a separate code of punishments.

The pattern lasted into the 1900s, as the page on Algeria in 1938 shows. It ended with the Algerian War of 1954 to 1962, after which most settlers left; see the exodus of the pieds-noirs.
